{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01EyC9HoYTfcbd72wa4Q3yrZ","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# EHNOTE, INC — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-15\n     4→Developer website: https://www.ehnote.com\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→EHNOTE, Inc is a small healthcare technology company founded in 2018, headquartered in Plano, Texas (also listing an address at 5050 Quorum Drive, Suite 700, Dallas, TX). The company was founded by Amarnatha Reddy Midde (CEO) and Amarnath Reddy Chappidi (COO), with Dr. Kuldeep Raizada listed as an advisor. The company has an estimated 61–100 employees and operates with a global team including development resources in India.\n     9→\n    10→EHNOTE builds a specialty-focused cloud EHR platform primarily targeting ophthalmology and eye care practices. The vendor claims to serve \"200+ Specialty Practices in USA & India.\" They participate in major medical conferences including AAO (American Academy of Ophthalmology), ASCRS, and HIMSS.\n    11→\n    12→Despite the SED intended user description on CHPL mentioning \"wound care physicians,\" the EHNOTE website makes no mention of wound care functionality. The product is overwhelmingly marketed as an ophthalmology EHR, with additional support for dental, gynecology, pediatrics, and general physician specialties. The wound care reference in the CHPL metadata is likely erroneous or reflects a testing scenario description rather than the product's actual market focus.\n    13→\n    14→## Product: EHNOTE\n    15→\n    16→CHPL IDs: 11356 (15.04.04.3171.EHNO.01.00.1.231025)\n    17→Certification date: 2023-10-25\n    18→Version: 1.0\n    19→\n    20→### What It Is\n    21→\n    22→EHNOTE is an all-in-one cloud-based EHR and practice management platform built primarily for ophthalmology practices. The vendor positions it as \"One Platform for Your Entire Ophthalmology Practice Ecosystem.\" The certified module appears to be the whole product — there is no indication of separate product lines or that the certification covers only a subset of the platform.\n    23→\n    24→The product spans multiple functional areas: clinical EHR, practice management, ambulatory surgery center (ASC) charting, optical point-of-sale, patient portal, telemedicine, revenue cycle management, and analytics. It also offers specialty modules for dental, gynecology, pediatrics, and general physician practices, though ophthalmology is the clear primary focus.\n    25→\n    26→The product relies on third-party components for certain functions: Carefluence Open API R4 for FHIR interoperability, DrFirst Rcopia for electronic prescribing, EMR Direct for secure email/Direct messaging, and Concurred for fax services (per the mandatory disclosures page).\n    27→\n    28→### Users & Market\n    29→\n    30→**Primary users**: Ophthalmologists, optometrists, opticians, and practice managers in eye care settings. The platform accommodates solo practitioners, independent practices, multi-location operations, and non-profit organizations.\n    31→\n    32→**Market size**: Small vendor — 200+ specialty practices in USA and India per the vendor's website. Only 1 user review found on SoftwareFinder (5 stars, October 2023). A few customer testimonials appear on the vendor website, with users reporting 3–4 years of product usage. Very limited independent review presence on third-party platforms.\n    33→\n    34→**Clinical settings**: Ambulatory ophthalmology clinics, optometry practices, optical retail locations, and ambulatory surgery centers. No hospital or inpatient presence described.\n    35→\n    36→**Go-to-market**: Direct sales, appears to target small-to-mid-size eye care practices. Presence at major ophthalmology and health IT conferences. International presence (India).\n    37→\n    38→### Modules & Functionality\n    39→\n    40→Based on vendor website and product pages, EHNOTE includes the following modules and capabilities:\n    41→\n    42→**Clinical EHR / Charting**\n    43→- Subspecialty-specific charting templates with auto-populating fields (per ophthalmology EHR page)\n    44→- Flexible one-page EHR and step-by-step EHR dashboards\n- General Physician: broad-based clinic management with labs and radiology integration\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on the described modules and features, EHNOTE stores and manages the document.body.appendChild(zi) : window.addEventListener('load', function () { document.body.appendChild(zi) });</script>\n    92→\n    93→</head>\n    94→\n    95→\n    96→<body ng-controller=\"MainCtrl\" class=\"mb-0\" ng-cloak>\n    97→\n    98→    <div id=\"preloader\"></div>\n    99→\n   100→    <i class=\"scroll-top scroll-top-mobile show fa fa-sort-asc\" id=\"Reloadpage\"></i>\n   101→\n   102→    <div ng-include=\"'../ehr/header'\"></div>\n   103→\n   104→\n   105→    <div class=\"view-container\">\n   106→        <section class=\"section-empty section-bg-f6f6f6\">\n   107→            <div class=\"container\">\n   108→                <div class=\"row\">\n   109→                    <div class=\"col-lg-12\">\n   110→                        <hr class=\"space l\">\n   111→                        <h1 class=\"text-h1 m-0\">Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export</h1>\n   112→                        <p class=\"text-label m-0 text-left\">Documentation Ehnote EHI Export</p>\n   113→                        <p class=\"text-h2 text-left\">Ehnote Inc.</p>\n   114→                        <ol class=\"list-sub-comb\" style=\"font-size: 16px;\">\n   115→                            <li>\n   116→                                <label>Introduction</label>\n   117→                                <p>\n   118→                                    PHI (Protected Health Information) can be exported from EHR (Electronic Health Record) systems,\n   119→                                    enabling efficient information sharing between healthcare providers while protecting patient privacy and\n   120→                                    security. Ehnote provides export file users with access to export format documentation so they may\n   121→                                    handle EHI after it has been exported using Ehnote\n   122→                                </p>\n   123→                                <p>\n   124→                                    The user will gain an understanding of the files that are produced by the PHI Export by using this\n   125→                                    documentation guide. It will provide further insight to ensure that this vast amount of information is\n   126→                                    used effectively, as well as instructions on how to read the files and comprehend the meaning of fields\n   127→                                    and connections.\n   128→                                </p>\n   129→                            </li>\n   130→                            <li>\n   131→                                <label>Understanding the Files</label>\n   132→                                <p>\n   133→                                    An export will include a single patient, depending on the specifications. All the files will be downloaded individually once\n   134→                                    the export and download button is clicked\n   135→                                </p>\n   136→                                <p>\n   137→                                    A number of files including patient <b>\n   138→                                        Investigations, Surgery consents, Referrals, Billings and Authorization files and Case\n   139→                                        history\n   140→                                    </b> can be found in this collection.\n   141→                                </p>\n   142→                                <ul style=\"list-style-type: lower-alpha\">\n   143→                                    <li>\n   144→                                        <label>PDF’s</label>\n   145→                                        <p>\n   146→                                            These files will be exported as a PDF file.\n   147→                                            The naming structure will be \"CaseSheet\" – represents it as a case sheet + BranchId - <span style=\"background-color: #FFFF00; padding: 3px\">_####</span> (clinic’s\n   148→                                            branch number) + Patientid – <span style=\"background-color: #00FF00; padding: 3px\">P####</span> + Appointmentdate - <span style=\"background-color: #00FFFF; padding: 3px\">A####</span> (Date of the appointment) +\n   149→                                            Filetype – <span style=\"background-color: #FF00FF; padding: 3px\">(.PDF)</span>\n   150→                                        </p>\n   151→                                        <ul style=\"margin-bottom: 5px;\">\n   152→                                            <li>\n   153→                                                <span style=\"background-color: #FFFF00; padding: 3px\">####</span> - BranchId\n   154→                                            </li>\n   155→                                            <li>\n   156→                                                <span style=\"background-color: #00FF00; padding: 3px\">P####</span> - PatientId\n   157→                                            </li>\n   158→                                            <li>\n   159→                                                <span style=\"background-color: #00FFFF; padding: 3px\">A####</span> - Appointment date\n   160→                                            </li>\n   161→                                            <li>\n   162→                                                <span style=\"background-color: #FF00FF; padding: 3px\">(.PDF)</span> – File type\n   163→                                            </li>\n   164→                                        </ul>\n   165→                                        <p>\n   166→                                            For example, CaseSheet_731P518612_A2023-12-08.pdf (731- Branch Id, 518612 – PatientId,\n   167→                                            2023-12-08 – Appointment date, .pdf – File type)\n   168→                                        </p>\n   169→                                    </li>\n   170→                                    <li>\n   171→                                        <label>Images</label>\n   172→                                        <p>\n   173→                                            These files will be exported in their native image format. Generally, but not limited to PNG, and\n   174→                                            JPEG.\n   175→                                        </p>\n   176→                                        <p>\n   177→                                            The naming structure will be Name<span style=\"background-color: #FFFF00; padding: 3px\">####</span>_<span style=\"background-color: #00FF00; padding: 3px\">P###</span><span style=\"background-color: #00FFFF; padding: 3px;\">_2023####</span>_ <span style=\"background-color: #FF00FF; padding: 3px\">.png</span>. Where <span style=\"background-color: #FFFF00; padding: 3px;\">###</span> is the patient name\n   178→                                            number, <span style=\"background-color: #00FF00; padding: 3px;\">P###</span> will be patient Id, <span style=\"background-color: #00FFFF\">2023####</span> is the date of file upload and <span style=\"background-color: #FF00FF; padding: 3px;\">.png</span> will be file name\n   179→                                        </p>\n   180→                                        <p>\n   181→                                            For example, <b>\n   182→                                                Alice_P2546_2023-01-08.PNG (Alice – Patient name, P2546 – Patient Id, 2023-01-08 –\n   183→                                                Appointment date, .png – File type).\n   184→                                            </b>\n   185→                                        </p>\n   186→                                    </li>\n   187→                                </ul>\n   188→                            </li>\n   189→                            <li>\n   190→                                <label>Linking the Files</label>\n   191→                                <p>\n   192→                                    Understanding how these files fit together to create a comprehensive picture for the resulting patient\n   193→                                    or patients) may be the most crucial aspect of using this collection of files. In summary, each file\n   194→                                    pertaining to a single patient will be shortened using the same P###_ patientidentifier, as previously\n   195→                                    mentioned.\n   196→                                </p>\n   197→                                <p>\n   198→                                    Taking a step down, and focusing on the PNG, JPEG and PDF files, it’s broken up into following\n   199→                                    categories. Investigations, Surgery consents, Referrals, Case sheets and Authorization file types.\n   200→                                </p>\n   201→                                <ul style=\"list-style: lower-alpha;\">\n   202→                                    <li>\n   203→                                        <label>Investigations, Surgery consents, Referrals and Authorization files:</label>\n   204→                                        <p>\n   205→                                            These are all the .JPEG and .PNG files where if the file type is “Surgery”, “Investigation”, “Referrals”\n   206→                                            or “Authorization”. One may refer to their special identification as a surgery or investigation. The\n   207→                                            Patient Identifier, where the extension \"P\"### will be used, is the crucial field.\n   208→                                        </p>\n   209→                                    </li>\n   210→                                    <li>\n   211→                                        <label>Patient case sheets:</label>\n   212→                                        <p>\n   213→                                            Patient case sheets are saved in .PDF formats, where patients entire clinical history for a particular\n   214→                                            appointment will be downloaded, The key field is the Patient Identifier where the extension “P”###\n   215→                                            will be followed with the Appointment date########\n   216→                                        </p>\n   217→                                    </li>\n   218→                                </ul>\n   219→                            </li>\n   220→                            <li>\n   221→                                <label>\n   222→                                    Understanding the Fields and Descriptions\n   223→                                </label>\n   224→                                <p>\n   225→                                    There is no \"one size fits all\" set of fields in the software because of the extensive customization that is possible.\n   226→                                    That being said, each primary PDF file that is exported will have a companion file.PNG as well.JPEG files were\n   227→                                    downloaded\n   228→                                </p>\n   229→                                <p>\n   230→                                    These files are basic image files with .JPEG, .PNG extension. In PDF’s each row will have a field names\n   231→                                    that related to the case history along with the clinical data represented\n   232→                                    For example, as part of the *_Patient.PDF:\n   233→                                </p>\n   234→                                <p>\n   235→                                    DATA: Name of the clinic, patient demographics, Chief complaints, Review of systems, Assessments, Medications and other clinical data part of the\n   236→                                    appointment\n   237→\n   238→                                </p>\n   239→                            </li>\n   240→                            <li>\n   241→                                <label>Usage Terms</label>\n   242→ document.body.appendChild(zi) : window.addEventListener('load', function () { document.body.appendChild(zi) });</script>\n\n</head>\n\n\n<body ng-controller=\"MainCtrl\" class=\"mb-0\" ng-cloak>\n\n    <div id=\"preloader\"></div>\n\n    <i class=\"scroll-top scroll-top-mobile show fa fa-sort-asc\" id=\"Reloadpage\"></i>\n\n    <div ng-include=\"'../ehr/header'\"></div>\n\n\n    <div class=\"view-container\">\n        <section class=\"section-empty section-bg-f6f6f6\">\n            <div class=\"container\">\n                <div class=\"row\">\n                    <div class=\"col-lg-12\">\n                        <hr class=\"space l\">\n                        <h1 class=\"text-h1 m-0\">Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export</h1>\n                        <p class=\"text-label m-0 text-left\">Documentation Ehnote EHI Export</p>\n                        <p class=\"text-h2 text-left\">Ehnote Inc.</p>\n                        <ol class=\"list-sub-comb\" style=\"font-size: 16px;\">\n                            <li>\n                                <label>Introduction</label>\n                                <p>\n                                    PHI (Protected Health Information) can be exported from EHR (Electronic Health Record) systems,\n                                    enabling efficient information sharing between healthcare providers while protecting patient privacy and\n                                    security. Ehnote provides export file users with access to export format documentation so they may\n                                    handle EHI after it has been exported using Ehnote\n                                </p>\n                                <p>\n                                    The user will gain an understanding of the files that are produced by the PHI Export by using this\n                                    documentation guide. It will provide further insight to ensure that this vast amount of information is\n                                    used effectively, as well as instructions on how to read the files and comprehend the meaning of fields\n                                    and connections.\n                                </p>\n                            </li>\n                            <li>\n                                <label>Understanding the Files</label>\n                                <p>\n                                    An export will include a single patient, depending on the specifications. All the files will be downloaded individually once\n                                    the export and download button is clicked\n                                </p>\n                                <p>\n                                    A number of files including patient <b>\n                                        Investigations, Surgery consents, Referrals, Billings and Authorization files and Case\n                                        history\n                                    </b> can be found in this collection.\n                                </p>\n                                <ul style=\"list-style-type: lower-alpha\">\n                                    <li>\n                                        <label>PDF’s</label>\n                                        <p>\n                                            These files will be exported as a PDF file.\n                                            The naming structure will be \"CaseSheet\" – represents it as a case sheet + BranchId - <span style=\"background-color: #FFFF00; padding: 3px\">_####</span> (clinic’s\n                                            branch number) + Patientid – <span style=\"background-color: #00FF00; padding: 3px\">P####</span> + Appointmentdate - <span style=\"background-color: #00FFFF; padding: 3px\">A####</span> (Date of the appointment) +\n                                            Filetype – <span style=\"background-color: #FF00FF; padding: 3px\">(.PDF)</span>\n                                        </p>\n                                        <ul style=\"margin-bottom: 5px;\">\n                                            <li>\n                                                <span style=\"background-color: #FFFF00; padding: 3px\">####</span> - BranchId\n                                            </li>\n                                            <li>\n                                                <span style=\"background-color: #00FF00; padding: 3px\">P####</span> - PatientId\n                                            </li>\n                                            <li>\n                                                <span style=\"background-color: #00FFFF; padding: 3px\">A####</span> - Appointment date\n                                            </li>\n                                            <li>\n                                                <span style=\"background-color: #FF00FF; padding: 3px\">(.PDF)</span> – File type\n                                            </li>\n                                        </ul>\n                                        <p>\n                                            For example, CaseSheet_731P518612_A2023-12-08.pdf (731- Branch Id, 518612 – PatientId,\n                                            2023-12-08 – Appointment date, .pdf – File type)\n                                        </p>\n                                    </li>\n                                    <li>\n                                        <label>Images</label>\n                                        <p>\n                                            These files will be exported in their native image format. Generally, but not limited to PNG, and\n                                            JPEG.\n                                        </p>\n                                        <p>\n                                            The naming structure will be Name<span style=\"background-color: #FFFF00; padding: 3px\">####</span>_<span style=\"background-color: #00FF00; padding: 3px\">P###</span><span style=\"background-color: #00FFFF; padding: 3px;\">_2023####</span>_ <span style=\"background-color: #FF00FF; padding: 3px\">.png</span>. Where <span style=\"background-color: #FFFF00; padding: 3px;\">###</span> is the patient name\n                                            number, <span style=\"background-color: #00FF00; padding: 3px;\">P###</span> will be patient Id, <span style=\"background-color: #00FFFF\">2023####</span> is the date of file upload and <span style=\"background-color: #FF00FF; padding: 3px;\">.png</span> will be file name\n                                        </p>\n                                        <p>\n                                            For example, <b>\n                                                Alice_P2546_2023-01-08.PNG (Alice – Patient name, P2546 – Patient Id, 2023-01-08 –\n                                                Appointment date, .png – File type).\n                                            </b>\n                                        </p>\n                                    </li>\n                                </ul>\n                            </li>\n                            <li>\n                                <label>Linking the Files</label>\n                                <p>\n                                    Understanding how these files fit together to create a comprehensive picture for the resulting patient\n                                    or patients) may be the most crucial aspect of using this collection of files. In summary, each file\n                                    pertaining to a single patient will be shortened using the same P###_ patientidentifier, as previously\n                                    mentioned.\n                                </p>\n                                <p>\n                                    Taking a step down, and focusing on the PNG, JPEG and PDF files, it’s broken up into following\n                                    categories. Investigations, Surgery consents, Referrals, Case sheets and Authorization file types.\n                                </p>\n                                <ul style=\"list-style: lower-alpha;\">\n                                    <li>\n                                        <label>Investigations, Surgery consents, Referrals and Authorization files:</label>\n                                        <p>\n                                            These are all the .JPEG and .PNG files where if the file type is “Surgery”, “Investigation”, “Referrals”\n                                            or “Authorization”. One may refer to their special identification as a surgery or investigation. The\n                                            Patient Identifier, where the extension \"P\"### will be used, is the crucial field.\n                                        </p>\n                                    </li>\n                                    <li>\n                                        <label>Patient case sheets:</label>\n                                        <p>\n                                            Patient case sheets are saved in .PDF formats, where patients entire clinical history for a particular\n                                            appointment will be downloaded, The key field is the Patient Identifier where the extension “P”###\n                                            will be followed with the Appointment date########\n                                        </p>\n                                    </li>\n                                </ul>\n                            </li>\n                            <li>\n                                <label>\n                                    Understanding the Fields and Descriptions\n                                </label>\n                                <p>\n                                    There is no \"one size fits all\" set of fields in the software because of the extensive customization that is possible.\n                                    That being said, each primary PDF file that is exported will have a companion file.PNG as well.JPEG files were\n                                    downloaded\n                                </p>\n                                <p>\n                                    These files are basic image files with .JPEG, .PNG extension. In PDF’s each row will have a field names\n                                    that related to the case history along with the clinical data represented\n                                    For example, as part of the *_Patient.PDF:\n                                </p>\n                                <p>\n                                    DATA: Name of the clinic, patient demographics, Chief complaints, Review of systems, Assessments, Medications and other clinical data part of the\n                                    appointment\n\n                                </p>\n {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01MSywvGeq3orHnCz7oyGBRz","type":"tool_result","content":[{"type":"text","text":"# take_snapshot response\n## Latest page snapshot\nuid=1_0 RootWebArea \"Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export\" url=\"https://ehnote.com/certification/ehi-export\"\n  uid=1_1 banner\n    uid=1_2 navigation\n      uid=1_3 StaticText \" +1 (747) 222 6099\"\n      uid=1_4 link \"info@ehnote.com\" url=\"mailto:info@ehnote.com\"\n        uid=1_5 StaticText \"info@ehnote.com\"\n      uid=1_6 link \"Facebook\" url=\"https://www.facebook.com/ehnote\"\n      uid=1_7 link \"Instagram\" url=\"https://www.instagram.com/ehnote_ehr/\"\n      uid=1_8 link \"Twitter\" url=\"https://twitter.com/Ehnote_\"\n      uid=1_9 link \"Youtube\" url=\"https://www.youtube.com/@ehnote9441\"\n      uid=1_10 link \"LinkedIn\" url=\"https://www.linkedin.com/company/ehnote/\"\n      uid=1_11 link \"logo\" url=\"https://ehnote.com/\"\n        uid=1_12 image \"logo\" url=\"https://ehnote.com/images/logo/logo-main.svg\"\n      uid=1_13 link \"Home\" url=\"https://ehnote.com/\"\n        uid=1_14 StaticText \"Home\"\n      uid=1_15 button \"Products \"\n      uid=1_16 button \"Resources\"\n      uid=1_17 button \"Company \"\n      uid=1_18 link \"Schedule a Demo\" url=\"https://ehnote.com/ehr/schedule-online-demo\"\n        uid=1_19 StaticText \"Schedule a Demo\"\n  uid=1_20 heading \"Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export\" level=\"1\"\n  uid=1_21 StaticText \"Documentation Ehnote EHI Export\"\n  uid=1_22 StaticText \"Ehnote Inc.\"\n  uid=1_23 StaticText \"Introduction\"\n  uid=1_24 StaticText \"PHI (Protected Health Information) can be exported from EHR (Electronic Health Record) systems, enabling efficient information sharing between healthcare providers while protecting patient privacy and security. Ehnote provides export file users with access to export format documentation so they may handle EHI after it has been exported using Ehnote\"\n  uid=1_25 StaticText \"The user will gain an understanding of the files that are produced by the PHI Export by using this documentation guide. It will provide further insight to ensure that this vast amount of information is used effectively, as well as instructions on how to read the files and comprehend the meaning of fields and connections.\"\n  uid=1_26 StaticText \"Understanding the Files\"\n  uid=1_27 StaticText \"An export will include a single patient, depending on the specifications. All the files will be downloaded individually once the export and download button is clicked\"\n  uid=1_28 StaticText \"A number of files including patient \"\n  uid=1_29 StaticText \"Investigations, Surgery consents, Referrals, Billings and Authorization files and Case history \"\n  uid=1_30 StaticText \"can be found in this collection.\"\n  uid=1_31 StaticText \"PDF’s\"\n  uid=1_32 StaticText \"These files will be exported as a PDF file. The naming structure will be \"CaseSheet\" – represents it as a case sheet + BranchId - \"\n  uid=1_33 StaticText \"_####\"\n  uid=1_34 StaticText \" (clinic’s branch number) + Patientid – \"\n  uid=1_35 StaticText \"P####\"\n  uid=1_36 StaticText \" + Appointmentdate - \"\n  uid=1_37 StaticText \"A####\"\n  uid=1_38 StaticText \" (Date of the appointment) + Filetype – \"\n  uid=1_39 StaticText \"(.PDF)\"\n  uid=1_40 StaticText \"####\"\n  uid=1_41 StaticText \" - BranchId\"\n  uid=1_42 StaticText \"P####\"\n  uid=1_43 StaticText \" - PatientId\"\n  uid=1_44 StaticText \"A####\"\n  uid=1_45 StaticText \" - Appointment date\"\n  uid=1_46 StaticText \"(.PDF)\"\n  uid=1_47 StaticText \" – File type\"\n  uid=1_48 StaticText \"For example, CaseSheet_731P518612_A2023-12-08.pdf (731- Branch Id, 518612 – PatientId, 2023-12-08 – Appointment date, .pdf – File type)\"\n  uid=1_49 StaticText \"Images\"\n  uid=1_50 StaticText \"These files will be exported in their native image format. Generally, but not limited to PNG, and JPEG.\"\n  uid=1_51 StaticText \"The naming structure will be Name\"\n  uid=1_52 StaticText \"####\"\n  uid=1_53 StaticText \"_\"\n  uid=1_54 StaticText \"P###\"\n  uid=1_55 StaticText \"_2023####\"\n  uid=1_56 StaticText \"_ \"\n  uid=1_57 StaticText \".png\"\n  uid=1_58 StaticText \". Where \"\n  uid=1_59 StaticText \"###\"\n  uid=1_60 StaticText \" is the patient name number, \"\n  uid=1_61 StaticText \"P###\"\n  uid=1_62 StaticText \" will be patient Id, \"\n  uid=1_63 StaticText \"2023####\"\n  uid=1_64 StaticText \" is the date of file upload and \"\n  uid=1_65 StaticText \".png\"\n  uid=1_66 StaticText \" will be file name\"\n  uid=1_67 StaticText \"For example, \"\n  uid=1_68 StaticText \"Alice_P2546_2023-01-08.PNG (Alice – Patient name, P2546 – Patient Id, 2023-01-08 – Appointment date, .png – File type).\"\n  uid=1_69 StaticText \"Linking the Files\"\n  uid=1_70 StaticText \"Understanding how these files fit together to create a comprehensive picture for the resulting patient or patients) may be the most crucial aspect of using this collection of files. In summary, each file pertaining to a single patient will be shortened using the same P###_ patientidentifier, as previously mentioned.\"\n  uid=1_71 StaticText \"Taking a step down, and focusing on the PNG, JPEG and PDF files, it’s broken up into following categories. Investigations, Surgery consents, Referrals, Case sheets and Authorization file types.\"\n  uid=1_72 StaticText \"Investigations, Surgery consents, Referrals and Authorization files:\"\n  uid=1_73 StaticText \"These are all the .JPEG and .PNG files where if the file type is “Surgery”, “Investigation”, “Referrals” or “Authorization”. One may refer to their special identification as a surgery or investigation. The Patient Identifier, where the extension \"P\"### will be used, is the crucial field.\"\n  uid=1_74 StaticText \"Patient case sheets:\"\n  uid=1_75 StaticText \"Patient case sheets are saved in .PDF formats, where patients entire clinical history for a particular appointment will be downloaded, The key field is the Patient Identifier where the extension “P”### will be followed with the Appointment date########\"\n  uid=1_76 StaticText \"Understanding the Fields and Descriptions\"\n  uid=1_77 StaticText \"There is no \"one size fits all\" set of fields in the software because of the extensive customization that is possible. That being said, each primary PDF file that is exported will have a companion file.PNG as well.JPEG files were downloaded\"\n  uid=1_78 StaticText \"These files are basic image files with .JPEG, .PNG extension. In PDF’s each row will have a field names that related to the case history along with the clinical data represented For example, as part of the *_Patient.PDF:\"\n  uid=1_79 StaticText \"DATA: Name of the clinic, patient demographics, Chief complaints, Review of systems, Assessments, Medications and other clinical data part of the appointment\"\n  uid=1_80 StaticText \"Usage Terms\"\n  uid=1_81 StaticText \"Definitions\"\n  uid=1_82 StaticText \"\"Ehnote Inc.\" may be referred to as \"we,\" \"our,\" or \"us\" in this Agreementand designates Ehnote Inc\"\n  uid=1_83 StaticText \"\"Healthcare Provider\" or \"our clients\" denotes Ehnote Inc. licensed and active users.\"\n  uid=1_84 StaticText \"\"You\" refers to any individual working on your behalf, as well as any workers or contractors employed by the company, as well as any other entity that views, uses, or obtains data through the API.\"\n  uid=1_85 StaticText \"Acceptance of Terms\"\n  uid=1_86 StaticText \"By accessing or utilizing Ehnote, you \"\n  uid=1_87 link \"accept the terms and conditions\" url=\"https://ehnote.com/certification/openapi-terms-conditions\"\n    uid=1_88 StaticText \"accept the terms and conditions\"\n  uid=1_89 StaticText \" stated herein, which together make up the \"Terms.\"\"\n  uid=1_90 StaticText \"Fees\"\n  uid=1_91 StaticText \"There are no extra costs associated with setting up, configuring, or accessing the API when using the Ehnote PHI Export as mentioned above.\"\n  uid=1_92 StaticText \"If the export size exceeds the contracted available size of your instance, there may be fees for clients hosted on our cloud instances for larger data storage requirements or IT support. Costs and Limitations are publicly available.\"\n  uid=1_93 StaticText \"Compliance with Laws and Regulations\"\n  uid=1_94 StaticText \"When using Ehnote, you must abide by all applicable laws, rules, and third-party rights. Additional grounds for removal consist of, but are not restricted to:\"\n  uid=1_98 StaticText \"Any protected connectivity content from the product may be shared or sublicensed for use by an unregistered application.\"\n  uid=1_99 StaticText \"Execute a task with the intention of exposing the interface to any malware, Trojan horses, worms, viruses, or other destructive objects.\"\n  uid=1_100 StaticText \"Defame, abuse, harass, stalk, or threaten others.\"\n  uid=1_101 StaticText \"Interfere with or disrupt the APIs or the servers or networks providing the APIs.\"\n  uid=1_102 StaticText \"Reverse engineer or make an attempt to extract the source code from any associated software or API, unless the applicable law expressly prohibits this restriction.\"\n  uid=1_103 StaticText \"Encourage illegal internet gaming or bothersome commercials or messaging.\"\n  uid=1_104 StaticText \"Eliminate, conceal, or modify the Ehnote terms of service or associated notifications.\"\n  uid=1_105 StaticText \"Collecting data outside the agree upon context of usage.\"\n  uid=1_106 StaticText \"Assigned credentials must be used solely for their intended purposes and within assignedaccess scopes.\"\n  uid=1_107 StaticText \"Security and Ownership\"\n  uid=1_108 StaticText \"A commercially reasonable effort must be made to safeguard any information, including personally identifiable information (\"PII\"), that your designee accesses. url=\"https://ehnote.com/ehr/schedule-online-demo\"\n        uid=1_19 StaticText \"Schedule a Demo\"\n  uid=1_20 heading \"Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export\" level=\"1\"\n  uid=1_21 StaticText \"Documentation Ehnote EHI Export\"\n  uid=1_22 StaticText \"Ehnote Inc.\"\n  uid=1_23 StaticText \"Introduction\"\n  uid=1_24 StaticText \"PHI (Protected Health Information) can be exported from EHR (Electronic Health Record) systems, enabling efficient information sharing between healthcare providers while protecting patient privacy and security. Ehnote provides export file users with access to export format documentation so they may handle EHI after it has been exported using Ehnote\"\n  uid=1_25 StaticText \"The user will gain an understanding of the files that are produced by the PHI Export by using this documentation guide. It will provide further insight to ensure that this vast amount of information is used effectively, as well as instructions on how to read the files and comprehend the meaning of fields and connections.\"\n  uid=1_26 StaticText \"Understanding the Files\"\n  uid=1_27 StaticText \"An export will include a single patient, depending on the specifications. All the files will be downloaded individually once the export and download button is clicked\"\n  uid=1_28 StaticText \"A number of files including patient \"\n  uid=1_29 StaticText \"Investigations, Surgery consents, Referrals, Billings and Authorization files and Case history \"\n  uid=1_30 StaticText \"can be found in this collection.\"\n  uid=1_31 StaticText \"PDF’s\"\n  uid=1_32 StaticText \"These files will be exported as a PDF file. The naming structure will be \"CaseSheet\" – represents it as a case sheet + BranchId - \"\n  uid=1_33 StaticText \"_####\"\n  uid=1_34 StaticText \" (clinic’s branch number) + Patientid – \"\n  uid=1_35 StaticText \"P####\"\n  uid=1_36 StaticText \" + Appointmentdate - \"\n  uid=1_37 StaticText \"A####\"\n  uid=1_38 StaticText \" (Date of the appointment) + Filetype – \"\n  uid=1_39 StaticText \"(.PDF)\"\n  uid=1_40 StaticText \"####\"\n  uid=1_41 StaticText \" - BranchId\"\n  uid=1_42 StaticText \"P####\"\n  uid=1_43 StaticText \" - PatientId\"\n  uid=1_44 StaticText \"A####\"\n  uid=1_45 StaticText \" - Appointment date\"\n  uid=1_46 StaticText \"(.PDF)\"\n  uid=1_47 StaticText \" – File type\"\n  uid=1_48 StaticText \"For example, CaseSheet_731P518612_A2023-12-08.pdf (731- Branch Id, 518612 – PatientId, 2023-12-08 – Appointment date, .pdf – File type)\"\n  uid=1_49 StaticText \"Images\"\n  uid=1_50 StaticText \"These files will be exported in their native image format. Generally, but not limited to PNG, and JPEG.\"\n  uid=1_51 StaticText \"The naming structure will be Name\"\n  uid=1_52 StaticText \"####\"\n  uid=1_53 StaticText \"_\"\n  uid=1_54 StaticText \"P###\"\n  uid=1_55 StaticText \"_2023####\"\n  uid=1_56 StaticText \"_ \"\n  uid=1_57 StaticText \".png\"\n  uid=1_58 StaticText \". Where \"\n  uid=1_59 StaticText \"###\"\n  uid=1_60 StaticText \" is the patient name number, \"\n  uid=1_61 StaticText \"P###\"\n  uid=1_62 StaticText \" will be patient Id, \"\n  uid=1_63 StaticText \"2023####\"\n  uid=1_64 StaticText \" is the date of file upload and \"\n  uid=1_65 StaticText \".png\"\n  uid=1_66 StaticText \" will be file name\"\n  uid=1_67 StaticText \"For example, \"\n  uid=1_68 StaticText \"Alice_P2546_2023-01-08.PNG (Alice – Patient name, P2546 – Patient Id, 2023-01-08 – Appointment date, .png – File type).\"\n  uid=1_69 StaticText \"Linking the Files\"\n  uid=1_70 StaticText \"Understanding how these files fit together to create a comprehensive picture for the resulting patient or patients) may be the most crucial aspect of using this collection of files. In summary, each file pertaining to a single patient will be shortened using the same P###_ patientidentifier, as previously mentioned.\"\n  uid=1_71 StaticText \"Taking a step down, and focusing on the PNG, JPEG and PDF files, it’s broken up into following categories. Investigations, Surgery consents, Referrals, Case sheets and Authorization file types.\"\n  uid=1_72 StaticText \"Investigations, Surgery consents, Referrals and Authorization files:\"\n  uid=1_73 StaticText \"These are all the .JPEG and .PNG files where if the file type is “Surgery”, “Investigation”, “Referrals” or “Authorization”. One may refer to their special identification as a surgery or investigation. The Patient Identifier, where the extension \"P\"### will be used, is the crucial field.\"\n  uid=1_74 StaticText \"Patient case sheets:\"\n  uid=1_75 StaticText \"Patient case sheets are saved in .PDF formats, where patients entire clinical history for a particular appointment will be downloaded, The key field is the Patient Identifier where the extension “P”### will be followed with the Appointment date########\"\n  uid=1_76 StaticText \"Understanding the Fields and Descriptions\"\n  uid=1_77 StaticText \"There is no \"one size fits all\" set of fields in the software because of the extensive customization that is possible. That being said, each primary PDF file that is exported will have a companion file.PNG as well.JPEG files were downloaded\"\n  uid=1_78 StaticText \"These files are basic image files with .JPEG, .PNG extension. In PDF’s each row will have a field names that related to the case history along with the clinical data represented For example, as part of the *_Patient.PDF:\"\n  uid=1_79 StaticText \"DATA: Name of the clinic, patient demographics, Chief complaints, Review of systems, Assessments, Medications and other clinical data part of the appointment\"\n  uid=1_80 StaticText \"Usage Terms\"\n  uid=1_81 StaticText \"Definitions\"\n  uid=1_82 StaticText \"\"Ehnote Inc.\" may be referred to as \"we,\" \"our,\" or \"us\" in this Agreementand designates Ehnote Inc\"\n  uid=1_83 StaticText \"\"Healthcare Provider\" or \"our clients\" denotes Ehnote Inc. licensed and active users.\"\n  uid=1_84 StaticText \"\"You\" refers to any individual working on your behalf, as well as any workers or contractors employed by the company, as well as any other entity that views, uses, or obtains data through the API.\"\n  uid=1_85 StaticText \"Acceptance of Terms\"\n  uid=1_86 StaticText \"By accessing or utilizing Ehnote, you \"\n  uid=1_87 link \"accept the terms and conditions\" url=\"https://ehnote.com/certification/openapi-terms-conditions\"\n    uid=1_88 StaticText \"accept the terms and conditions\"\n  uid=1_89 StaticText \" stated herein, which together make up the \"Terms.\"\"\n  uid=1_90 StaticText \"Fees\"\n  uid=1_91 StaticText \"There are no extra costs associated with setting up, configuring, or accessing the API when using the Ehnote PHI Export as mentioned above.\"\n  uid=1_92 StaticText \"If the export size exceeds the contracted available size of your instance, there may be fees for clients hosted on our cloud instances for larger data storage requirements or IT support. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01X4K2KLSThuVZBM2jREqQV6","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_012aWFBSEWcMmHAc7jx4xcYA","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/ehnote-inc--ehnote/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# EHNOTE, INC — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-15\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://ehnote.com/certification/ehi-export\n- CHPL IDs: 11356 (15.04.04.3171.EHNO.01.00.1.231025)\n- Certification date: 2023-10-25\n- Product: EHNOTE v1.0\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n### Step 1: Probe the registered URL\n```bash\ncurl -sI -L \"https://ehnote.com/certification/ehi-export\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36'\n```\nResult: HTTP 200, `Content-Type: text/html`, served via Cloudflare. No redirects. Last-Modified: 2025-06-03.\n\n### Step 2: Fetch and examine the page\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://ehnote.com/certification/ehi-export\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o ehi-export-page.html\n```\nResult: 31,265 bytes of static HTML. AngularJS-based page (`ng-app=\"myapp\"`) but the EHI export content is rendered server-side in the HTML — no dynamic content loading required.\n\n### Step 3: Search for downloadable files\n```bash\ngrep -oiE 'href=\"[^\"]*\\.(pdf|zip|xlsx|xls|csv|json|doc|docx|yaml|yml)[^\"]*\"' ehi-export-page.html\n```\nResult: **No downloadable files found.** The page contains zero links to PDFs, ZIPs, CSVs, JSON schemas, or any other downloadable documentation artifacts. The only outbound link is to the terms and conditions page (`https://ehnote.com/certification/openapi-terms-conditions`).\n\n### Step 4: Check the mandatory disclosures / certification page\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://ehnote.com/certification/certification-link.html\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o cert-page.html\n```\nResult: 24,291 bytes. Contains links to Real-World Testing PDFs, a compliance certificate, and a risk mitigation PDF — none related to EHI export documentation, data dictionaries, or export format specifications.\n\n### Step 5: Check footer links for related content\nThe footer of the EHI export page includes a \"Compliances\" section with links to:\n- Certifications (certification-link page)\n- FHIR END POINT (fhir-endpoints)\n- SMART ON FHIR (fhir-api)\n- API Documentation (https://openapi.ehnote.com/ — a Postman collection for FHIR API)\n- FHIR API Terms and Conditions\n- Developer Login (https://interop.ehnote.com/admin/console/auth — login wall)\n- EHI Export (this page)\n\nThe API documentation at openapi.ehnote.com is a Postman-hosted FHIR API collection — this is for the (g)(10) standardized FHIR API, not the (b)(10) EHI export. The FHIR API page makes no mention of EHI or b(10) export.\n\n### Step 6: Browser verification\nLoaded the page in Chrome to verify no JavaScript-rendered content was missed. The page renders identically to the curl-fetched HTML. No expandable sections, accordions, or dynamically loaded content. Screenshots captured.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe entire EHI export documentation consists of a single static HTML page at the registered URL. There are no downloadable files, no data dictionary, no schema, no API specification, and no sample export files.\n\n### Export Format\n\nThe export produces **individual files per patient**, downloaded when the user clicks an \"export and download\" button in the EHR. The exported files are:\n\n1. **PDF case sheets** — One PDF per appointment per patient, containing the clinical history for that visit. Naming convention: `CaseSheet_{BranchId}P{PatientId}_A{AppointmentDate}.pdf`\n   - Example: `CaseSheet_731P518612_A2023-12-08.pdf`\n   - Content described as: \"Name of the clinic, patient demographics, Chief complaints, Review of systems, Assessments, Medications and other clinical data part of the appointment\"\n\n2. **Image files (PNG/JPEG)** — Companion images exported alongside PDFs. These represent investigations, surgery consents, referrals, and authorization documents. Naming convention: `{PatientName}_P{PatientId}_{Date}.{ext}`\n   - Example: `Alice_P2546_2023-01-08.PNG`\n\n### File Categories\n\nThe documentation lists these categories of exported data:\n- **Investigations** — image files (JPEG/PNG)\n- **Surgery consents** — image files (JPEG/PNG)\n- **Referrals** — image files (JPEG/PNG)\n- **Billings and Authorization files** — image files (JPEG/PNG)\n- **Case history / Case sheets** — PDF files\n\n### Data Fields\n\nThe documentation explicitly states: *\"There is no 'one size fits all' set of fields in the software because of the extensive customization that is possible.\"* It describes PDF field content only at a very high level: \"each row will have a field names that related to the case history along with the clinical data represented.\"\n\nThe DATA section for PDFs is described as containing: \"Name of the clinic, patient demographics, Chief complaints, Review of systems, Assessments, Medications and other clinical data part of the appointment.\"\n\n### Linking Mechanism\n\nFiles for the same patient are linked by a shared `P####` patient identifier in the filename. Files for the same appointment share both the patient ID and appointment date in the naming convention.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nBased on the product research, EHNOTE stores extensive data across clinical, administrative, billing, optical retail, patient engagement, telemedicine, and analytics domains. The EHI export documentation describes a very narrow subset:\n\n**Mentioned in the export documentation:**\n- Patient demographics (mentioned in case sheet PDF content)\n- Chief complaints (mentioned)\n- Review of systems (mentioned)\n- Assessments (mentioned)\n- Medications (mentioned)\n- Clinical visit data (\"other clinical data part of the appointment\")\n- Surgery consents (as image files)\n- Investigations / diagnostic data (as image files)\n- Referrals (as image files)\n- Billing / authorization files (as image files — though the documentation is vague about what \"billing\" content is actually exported)\n\n**Absent or not mentioned from the product's known data domains:**\n- **Ophthalmic-specific data**: Visual acuity measurements, IOP readings, refraction data, DICOM images, anatomical drawings — the core specialty data for this ophthalmology-focused EHR is not specifically addressed\n- **Prescriptions / e-prescribing records**: No mention of prescription data export\n- **Lab results / diagnostic reports**: Not specifically mentioned (may fall under \"Investigations\" but unclear)\n- **Immunization records**: Not mentioned\n- **Problem lists / allergy lists**: Not specifically mentioned (may be in case sheet PDFs)\n- **Care plans / goals**: Not mentioned\n- **Patient portal communications**: Secure messages, patient-submitted forms/images\n- **Telemedicine session records**: Not mentioned\n- **Optical retail / POS data**: Inventory, orders, lens prescriptions not mentioned\n- **Insurance / enrollment data**: Not specifically addressed\n- **Claims / financial transactions**: The documentation says \"Billings and Authorization files\" exist but provides no detail on format or content\n- **ASC surgical documentation**: Pre-op, intra-op, post-op, anesthesia records not specifically mentioned (surgery \"consents\" are mentioned, but not the full surgical record)\n- **Specialty module data**: Dental charts, gynecology records, pediatric growth charts\n- **Patient CRM data**: Lead tracking, counseling notes, quotations\n\nThe core concern is that this export appears to be appointment-centric PDFs and related images — essentially a printout of the visit record. There is no indication that it exports the full breadth of structured data the system stores.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses **PDFs and image files** — the least computable format possible. This is essentially a \"print to PDF\" export of clinical encounter records plus scanned/attached document images.\n\n- No structured data format (no FHIR, no C-CDA, no CSV, no JSON, no XML, no SQL dump)\n- No machine-readable schema or data dictionary\n- No API endpoint for bulk data extraction\n- The PDF format means that extracting individual data elements (diagnoses, medications, vitals, etc.) requires OCR or PDF parsing — the structured data that exists in the EHR database is flattened into rendered documents\n- A third party could not reconstruct a patient record programmatically from this export; they could only read PDFs and look at images\n\nThe (b)(10) requirement asks for export of all electronic health information. While there's no format mandate, exporting only as PDFs means the structured nature of the data is lost. A medication list in a PDF is fundamentally less useful than a structured medication list in any computable format.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThe documentation is **minimal and vague**:\n\n- **No data dictionary**: There is no field-level documentation of what data is in the exported PDFs or images. The documentation explicitly acknowledges this gap: \"There is no 'one size fits all' set of fields.\"\n- **No schema or format specification**: Beyond the file naming convention, there is no specification of what the PDFs contain or how they are structured.\n- **No sample export files**: No examples of what an exported PDF looks like or what data fields are included.\n- **No export instructions**: The documentation says files are \"downloaded individually once the export and download button is clicked\" but provides no step-by-step guide, screenshots of the export interface, or user workflow documentation.\n- **No worked examples**: Beyond the file naming examples, there are no examples of actual export content.\n- The documentation reads as a compliance checkbox rather than a practical technical guide. A developer or data analyst receiving these exported PDFs would have essentially no guidance on what data to expect or how to process it.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Field-level documentation**: None. The documentation only names broad categories (demographics, complaints, assessments, medications) without defining specific fields, data types, value sets, or structures.\n- **Value sets / coded fields**: Not documented at all.\n- **Relationships between entities**: Described only by filename convention (patient ID links files together).\n- **Versioning**: None visible. The page was last modified 2025-06-03.\n- **Completeness**: The documentation is essentially a 2-page description of file naming conventions plus legal boilerplate (terms of use, liability, etc.). The substantive technical content is approximately 500 words.\n\n### Overall Assessment\n\nEHNOTE's EHI export documentation is among the most minimal possible. The export itself appears to be a per-patient, per-appointment PDF dump with associated image attachments — essentially what you would get if you printed the patient chart to PDF. While this captures the rendered clinical information visible to users, it:\n\n1. **Loses all structure**: Structured data (diagnoses coded in ICD-11, medications, vitals, etc.) becomes unstructured text in a PDF\n2. **Covers only clinical encounters**: There's no evidence that billing records, optical retail data, patient portal content, telemedicine sessions, or specialty-specific structured data (visual acuity measurements, IOP trends, etc.) are included\n3. **Provides no data dictionary**: The documentation explicitly acknowledges the lack of standardized field definitions due to \"extensive customization\"\n4. **Has no computable artifacts**: No schema, API spec, CSV template, or any machine-readable documentation\n\nThis is a small vendor (200+ practices) with a certification from October 2023. The export approach and documentation appear to represent minimal compliance effort rather than a thoughtful approach to health information portability.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://ehnote.com/certification/ehi-export\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (static HTML works with curl)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none (Cloudflare in pass-through mode, no challenge)\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- No obstacles encountered accessing the documentation\n- The `/certification/` index page returns \"You do not have permission to view this directory or page\" — but the specific EHI export URL works fine\n- The certification disclosures page was checked for additional EHI-related links — none found\n- The openapi.ehnote.com Postman API documentation was verified to be FHIR (g)(10) API docs, not related to the (b)(10) EHI export\n- No downloadable files exist on the EHI export page — the entire documentation is inline HTML text\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":218,"cache_read_input_tokens":60479,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":218},"output_tokens":25,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"ff57f93e-d371-4aeb-9204-2ec4c7936bf1","uuid":"785e82ca-6762-48ad-8f00-3e46e3758ca4"}

Contains links to Real-World Testing PDFs, a compliance certificate, and a risk mitigation PDF — none related to EHI export documentation, data dictionaries, or export format specifications.\n\n### Step 5: Check footer links for related content\nThe footer of the EHI export page includes a \"Compliances\" section with links to:\n- Certifications (certification-link page)\n- FHIR END POINT (fhir-endpoints)\n- SMART ON FHIR (fhir-api)\n- API Documentation (https://openapi.ehnote.com/ — a Postman collection for FHIR API)\n- FHIR API Terms and Conditions\n- Developer Login (https://interop.ehnote.com/admin/console/auth — login wall)\n- EHI Export (this page)\n\nThe API documentation at openapi.ehnote.com is a Postman-hosted FHIR API collection — this is for the (g)(10) standardized FHIR API, not the (b)(10) EHI export. The FHIR API page makes no mention of EHI or b(10) export.\n\n### Step 6: Browser verification\nLoaded the page in Chrome to verify no JavaScript-rendered content was missed. The page renders identically to the curl-fetched HTML. No expandable sections, accordions, or dynamically loaded content. Screenshots captured.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe entire EHI export documentation consists of a single static HTML page at the registered URL. There are no downloadable files, no data dictionary, no schema, no API specification, and no sample export files.\n\n### Export Format\n\nThe export produces **individual files per patient**, downloaded when the user clicks an \"export and download\" button in the EHR. The exported files are:\n\n1. **PDF case sheets** — One PDF per appointment per patient, containing the clinical history for that visit. Naming convention: `CaseSheet_{BranchId}P{PatientId}_A{AppointmentDate}.pdf`\n   - Example: `CaseSheet_731P518612_A2023-12-08.pdf`\n   - Content described as: \"Name of the clinic, patient demographics, Chief complaints, Review of systems, Assessments, Medications and other clinical data part of the appointment\"\n\n2. **Image files (PNG/JPEG)** — Companion images exported alongside PDFs. These represent investigations, surgery consents, referrals, and authorization documents. Naming convention: `{PatientName}_P{PatientId}_{Date}.{ext}`\n   - Example: `Alice_P2546_2023-01-08.PNG`\n\n### File Categories\n\nThe documentation lists these categories of exported data:\n- **Investigations** — image files (JPEG/PNG)\n- **Surgery consents** — image files (JPEG/PNG)\n- **Referrals** — image files (JPEG/PNG)\n- **Billings and Authorization files** — image files (JPEG/PNG)\n- **Case history / Case sheets** — PDF files\n\n### Data Fields\n\nThe documentation explicitly states: *\"There is no 'one size fits all' set of fields in the software because of the extensive customization that is possible.\"* It describes PDF field content only at a very high level: \"each row will have a field names that related to the case history along with the clinical data represented.\"\n\nThe DATA section for PDFs is described as containing: \"Name of the clinic, patient demographics, Chief complaints, Review of systems, Assessments, Medications and other clinical data part of the appointment.\"\n\n### Linking Mechanism\n\nFiles for the same patient are linked by a shared `P####` patient identifier in the filename. Files for the same appointment share both the patient ID and appointment date in the naming convention.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nBased on the product research, EHNOTE stores extensive data across clinical, administrative, billing, optical retail, patient engagement, telemedicine, and analytics domains. The EHI export documentation describes a very narrow subset:\n\n**Mentioned in the export documentation:**\n- Patient demographics (mentioned in case sheet PDF content)\n- Chief complaints (mentioned)\n- Review of systems (mentioned)\n- Assessments (mentioned)\n- Medications (mentioned)\n- Clinical visit data (\"other clinical data part of the appointment\")\n- Surgery consents (as image files)\n- Investigations / diagnostic data (as image files)\n- Referrals (as image files)\n- Billing / authorization files (as image files — though the documentation is vague about what \"billing\" content is actually exported)\n\n**Absent or not mentioned from the product's known data domains:**\n- **Ophthalmic-specific data**: Visual acuity measurements, IOP readings, refraction data, DICOM images, anatomical drawings — the core specialty data for this ophthalmology-focused EHR is not specifically addressed\n- **Prescriptions / e-prescribing records**: No mention of prescription data export\n- **Lab results / diagnostic reports**: Not specifically mentioned (may fall under \"Investigations\" but unclear)\n- **Immunization records**: Not mentioned\n- **Problem lists / allergy lists**: Not specifically mentioned (may be in case sheet PDFs)\n- **Care plans / goals**: Not mentioned\n- **Patient portal communications**: Secure messages, patient-submitted forms/images\n- **Telemedicine session records**: Not mentioned\n- **Optical retail / POS data**: Inventory, orders, lens prescriptions not mentioned\n- **Insurance / enrollment data**: Not specifically addressed\n- **Claims / financial transactions**: The documentation says \"Billings and Authorization files\" exist but provides no detail on format or content\n- **ASC surgical documentation**: Pre-op, intra-op, post-op, anesthesia records not specifically mentioned (surgery \"consents\" are mentioned, but not the full surgical record)\n- **Specialty module data**: Dental charts, gynecology records, pediatric growth charts\n- **Patient CRM data**: Lead tracking, counseling notes, quotations\n\nThe core concern is that this export appears to be appointment-centric PDFs and related images — essentially a printout of the visit record. There is no indication that it exports the full breadth of structured data the system stores.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses **PDFs and image files** — the least computable format possible. This is essentially a \"print to PDF\" export of clinical encounter records plus scanned/attached document images.\n\n- No structured data format (no FHIR, no C-CDA, no CSV, no JSON, no XML, no SQL dump)\n- No machine-readable schema or data dictionary\n- No API endpoint for bulk data extraction\n- The PDF format means that extracting individual data elements (diagnoses, medications, vitals, etc.) requires OCR or PDF parsing — the structured data that exists in the EHR database is flattened into rendered documents\n- A third party could not reconstruct a patient record programmatically from this export; they could only read PDFs and look at images\n\nThe (b)(10) requirement asks for export of all electronic health information. While there's no format mandate, exporting only as PDFs means the structured nature of the data is lost. A medication list in a PDF is fundamentally less useful than a structured medication list in any computable format.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThe documentation is **minimal and vague**:\n\n- **No data dictionary**: There is no field-level documentation of what data is in the exported PDFs or images. The documentation explicitly acknowledges this gap: \"There is no 'one size fits all' set of fields.\"\n- **No schema or format specification**: Beyond the file naming convention, there is no specification of what the PDFs contain or how they are structured.\n- **No sample export files**: No examples of what an exported PDF looks like or what data fields are included.\n- **No export instructions**: The documentation says files are \"downloaded individually once the export and download button is clicked\" but provides no step-by-step guide, screenshots of the export interface, or user workflow documentation.\n- **No worked examples**: Beyond the file naming examples, there are no examples of actual export content.\n- The documentation reads as a compliance checkbox rather than a practical technical guide. A developer or data analyst receiving these exported PDFs would have essentially no guidance on what data to expect or how to process it.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Field-level documentation**: None. The documentation only names broad categories (demographics, complaints, assessments, medications) without defining specific fields, data types, value sets, or structures.\n- **Value sets / coded fields**: Not documented at all.\n- **Relationships between entities**: Described only by filename convention (patient ID links files together).\n- **Versioning**: None visible. The page was last modified 2025-06-03.\n- **Completeness**: The documentation is essentially a 2-page description of file naming conventions plus legal boilerplate (terms of use, liability, etc.). The substantive technical content is approximately 500 words.\n\n### Overall Assessment\n\nEHNOTE's EHI export documentation is among the most minimal possible. The export itself appears to be a per-patient, per-appointment PDF dump with associated image attachments — essentially what you would get if you printed the patient chart to PDF. While this captures the rendered clinical information visible to users, it:\n\n1. **Loses all structure**: Structured data (diagnoses coded in ICD-11, medications, vitals, etc.) becomes unstructured text in a PDF\n2. **Covers only clinical encounters**: There's no evidence that billing records, optical retail data, patient portal content, telemedicine sessions, or specialty-specific structured data (visual acuity measurements, IOP trends, etc.) are included\n3. **Provides no data dictionary**: The documentation explicitly acknowledges the lack of standardized field definitions due to \"extensive customization\"\n4. **Has no computable artifacts**: No schema, API spec, CSV template, or any machine-readable documentation\n\nThis is a small vendor (200+ practices) with a certification from October 2023. The export approach and documentation appear to represent minimal compliance effort rather than a thoughtful approach to health information portability.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://ehnote.com/certification/ehi-export\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (static HTML works with curl)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none (Cloudflare in pass-through mode, no challenge)\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- No obstacles encountered accessing the documentation\n- The `/certification/` index page returns \"You do not have permission to view this directory or page\" — but the specific EHI export URL works fine\n- The certification disclosures page was checked for additional EHI-related links — none found\n- The openapi.ehnote.com Postman API documentation was verified to be FHIR (g)(10) API docs, not related to the (b)(10) EHI export\n- No downloadable files exist on the EHI export page — the entire documentation is inline HTML text\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null}}
